newsitem.title: USA: First State sets shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: First State sets shareholder rights plan.

text.p: First State Bancorporation said on Tuesday its board approved a shareholder rights plan to assure fair treatment for its shareholders if there is a takeover attempt.

The plan, which is not a response to any existing effort to acquire control of the company, provides a dividend distribution of one right for each share held at the close of business on November 20, 1996, First State said.
The rights will become exercisable only if a person or group accumulates 10 percent or more of First State's common shares, First state said.

First State said the rights, which will expire October 25, 2006, will entitle holders to buy the common stock of First State or a party attempting to take over the commercial bank holding company at half the market value.
In addition, the board may, at its option, exchange part or all of the rights for common shares of First State on a one-for-one basis, the company said.
